coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Rock Square
record.summary: The neighborhood's planned central park of about 1.1 acres (1.32 acres, 57,626 sq ft, in the March 2012 proposal), an urban green framed by Blocks E and F with a lawn, a plaza with an interactive spray ground, a cafe pavilion and a tree bosque with retail kiosks; the Design Controls require wind protection, public restrooms and preserved water views. The Draft EIR includes a 700-space garage beneath it. Unbuilt as of the Port's June 2026 Phase 2 update, which describes the site as a surface parking lot and puts Phase 2 in pre-development.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt public square) on the undivided remainder lot 8719A006. North edge is a recorded lot line (~0 m); the other three edges come from the Design Controls figure through a 0.7 m RMS transform (~1-3 m). Traced area 47,724 sf, smaller than the 57,626 sf the 2012 proposal gave -- the tracing is logged in this shape's data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record). The July 2019 Phase 1 submittal planned 'two interim pedestrian plazas south of Parcels B and F'; no source read confirms that an interim plaza was built or where it sits, and the Port's June 2026 update describes the site as a surface parking lot.
notes.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls, Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151) and Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); north edge is Verde's recorded lot line (8719C001), south edge is Block E's traced north edge.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this square -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so mapping each block from that lot would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this square touches them.
notes.regulatory_context: Dedicated public open space (Design Controls Chapter 3, Section 3.3). Directly framed by Block F/Verde (north) and Block E (south), with the Shared Public Way (west) and Bridgeview Street (east) along its sides; Blocks B, C, I and J are also one street removed (Design Controls Figure 6.2). The Design Controls text states no acreage; the Port's January 2018 approvals report gives 1.1 acres ('a 1.1 acre neighborhood central gathering place called Mission Rock Square'), which matches this record's traced figure; the March 2012 Revised Proposal's parcel table gave 57,626 sf (1.32 ac) for an earlier, deeper layout.

facts.value: 57,626 sq ft / 1.32 acres (March 2012 Revised Proposal parcel summary); the Port's January 2018 approvals memo describes it as 1.1 acres

Public open space. March 2012 Revised Proposal (the developer's proposal, not an adopted plan): urban neighborhood park with multi-use lawn, plaza with interactive spray ground, cafe pavilion, bosque with retail kiosks and an arts program site. Adopted Design Controls (Sec. 3.3): a civic 'living room' square with a large flexible open area for temporary uses and events, wind protection through tree planting, one permanent retail and food structure with public restrooms, at least one stormwater treatment garden, and views to the Bay maintained
Protected from wind; public restrooms required; at least one iconic feature; views to the water maintained through the square; ground-floor uses on Blocks E and F to engage it
Framed by Block F (Verde, north) and Block E (south); Blocks C and I are one street away across the Shared Public Way and Bridgeview Street
A below-grade garage of up to 700 spaces (227,200 gsf) is permitted beneath the square in combination with the Block D2 structure
Port of San Francisco; parks and open spaces at Mission Rock remain Port-owned
Named in the Design Controls as a centralized stormwater treatment location
Port of San Francisco (Seawall Lot 337); future parcel to be ground-leased for 75 years under the DDA
Seawall Lot 337 Associates, LLC (San Francisco Giants and Tishman Speyer), master developer with an option on each vertical parcel

changes.text: Mission Rock Square's record and map shape now say: the planned size is about 1.1 acres (the Port's 2018 report; the 1.32 acres / 57,626 sq ft figure is from the March 2012 proposal), and the program quoted from the 2012 proposal is labelled as such alongside what the adopted Design Controls (Sec. 3.3) require. The sentence saying an interim plaza built with Phase 1 occupies the north part was removed (the 2019 submittal only planned two interim plazas south of Parcels B and F); 'unbuilt' is dated to the Port's June 2026 update; the Draft EIR garage is no longer called optional; Blocks B and J are added to the blocks one street from the square; the statements that the lots match the plan within 3% and that the square is an 'elongated hexagon' are corrected or flagged in a new dated note; the Jan 30, 2018, Oct 10, 2023 and March 11, 2025 Port Commission actions cite the minutes and misquoted wording was corrected; and source citations were fixed. The shape is unchanged.

open_questions: Which phase will deliver the square and whether the below-grade garage option survives: not stated in any Port memo read; the Phase 2 Garage Report was not located.
Cost of the square: none published. Phase 1's China Basin Park inland budget ($39-41M) is the only comparable figure in the Port memos.

The 1.1-acre figure in the 2018 approvals memo versus 1.32 acres in the March 2012 proposal is unexplained; the traced shape on this record's map is about 1.57 acres after clipping, per its own accuracy note.
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Mission Rock Square. The DDA (lodged with the Board of Supervisors 2/1/2018, Board File 180092, adopted as Resolution 42-18, effective 8/15/2018) was read in full: its Land Use Table (DDA Section 1.5) assigns a Phase only to Development Parcels, not to the Square, which its Infrastructure Plan (DDA Exhibit B3, Section 1.8) instead ties to 'associated' Development Parcels -- here Block F (built in Phase 1) and Block E (Phase 3, per that record). Its Exhibit B2 Schedule of Performance gives a 2018 'Target Date' of August 2024 for completing Phase 3's horizontal Phase Improvements, already elapsed with the earlier Phase 2 still not begun as of the October 2023 'not currently financially feasible' finding in this record's own milestones. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all. No later Port memo or news source gives a revised target year for Phase 3, for the square specifically, or for the Project's full buildout, so no basis (record, phase or project) supports a non-elapsed date.
